	Domain: telecom
	Reason for call:
		Your phone has been showing 'No Service' for the past few hours.
	Known info:
		You are John Smith with phone number 555-123-2002.
	Task instructions:
		If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You will consider the issue resolved when the status bar shows that you have signal. Always check the status bar if the agent asks you for status information. If the agent asks you to pay a bill, you accept. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
		Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
		For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
		Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
		If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

turns.thought:
Your line is back up. Here's the confirmation:

**Payment:** Bill **B1234321** — $65.00 — status is now **Paid**.

**Line 555-123-2002:** status is now **Active**, and the suspension start date has been cleared.

The billing suspension is fully lifted. Now please **reboot your device** (power it off completely, wait a few seconds, then power it back on). That's required for the service to re-register on the network — you should have bars and full service within a couple of minutes.

If you're still showing "No Service" after the reboot, let me know and we'll keep troubleshooting (we'd look at things like Airplane Mode, your SIM card, and your APN settings).

One last reminder so this doesn't happen again: bill **B1002** for **$150.00** (February charges) is issued and was due 2025-02-19. That one isn't blocking service right now, but it will go overdue soon — worth taking care of at your earliest convenience.

Good news first: from our side, your line is confirmed **Active** and the billing suspension is completely cleared — so there's nothing on the account blocking service anymore.

The remaining problem is on the phone itself. Airplane Mode turns off all the wireless radios (cellular, Wi‑Fi, Bluetooth), which is why you're seeing no signal bars even though your line is live.

Please turn it off:

1. **Quickest way:** Swipe down from the top of the screen (twice on some phones) to open Quick Settings, then tap the **✈️ Airplane Mode** tile so it turns gray/off.
2. **Or via Settings:** Settings → **Network & Internet** (or "Connections" on Samsung) → toggle **Airplane Mode** to **Off**.

Once it's off:
- The airplane icon should disappear from your status bar.
- Give it about 30–60 seconds to re-register on the network, and you should see signal bars plus your network type (e.g. 5G / LTE) come back.

Turn it off and tell me what your status bar shows afterward — whether the airplane icon is gone and whether you now have signal bars. If you get bars but mobile data still isn't working, or you still have no signal at all, I'll walk you through the next steps (SIM check and APN settings).
